shloka_text: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरो ऽभिहितो मया । यद्यस्ति श्रवणे श्रद्धा शृणुष्वेहापरां कथाम् ।। 7.55.1 ।।
transliteration: eṣa te nṛgaśāpasya vistaro 'bhihito mayā | yadyasti śravaṇe śraddhā śṛṇuṣvehāparāṃ kathām || 7.55.1 ||
translation: एषः this, ते to you, नृगशापस्य of Nṛga's curse, विस्तरः the detailed account, अभिहितः has been told, मया by me, यदि if, अस्ति there is, श्रवणे in listening, श्रद्धा faith/desire, शृणुष्व listen, इह here, अपराम् another, कथाम् story.
explanation: I have told you this detailed account of Nṛga's curse; if you have a desire to listen, then hear another story here.
comments: At Lakshmana's wish Rama tells of King Nimi of the Ikshvakus, who founds a city near Gautama's hermitage and begins a long sacrifice -- choosing Vasishtha, who being already engaged by Indra bids him wait, Nimi has Gautama officiate instead -- returning to find himself passed over and the sleeping king failing to receive him, the angered Vasishtha curses Nimi to lose his body, Nimi curses him in return, and both become bodiless.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सौमित्रिः पुनरब्रवीत् । तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे नृप ।। 7.55.2 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu rāmeṇa saumitriḥ punarabravīt | tṛptirāścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ nāsti me nṛpa || 7.55.2 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामेण by Rama, सौमित्रिः Saumitri (Lakshmana), पुनः again, अब्रवीत् spoke, तृप्तिः satisfaction, आश्चर्यभूतानाम् of wonderful, कथानाम् stories, न not, अस्ति is, मे to me, नृप O king.
explanation: But thus spoken to by Rama, Saumitri spoke again, saying, "O king, I have no satisfaction from wonderful stories."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । कथां परमधर्मिष्ठां व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.3 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāma ikṣvākunandanaḥ | kathāṃ paramadharmiṣṭhāṃ vyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.3 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामः Rama, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvakus, कथाम् a story, परमधर्मिष्ठाम् most righteous, व्याहर्तुम् to narrate, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: But thus spoken to by Lakshmana, Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, began to narrate a most righteous story.

shloka_text: आसीद्राजा निमिर्नाम इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः ।। 7.55.4 ।।
transliteration: āsīdrājā nimirnāma ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām | putro dvādaśamo vīrye dharme ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ || 7.55.4 ||
translation: आसीत् was, राजा a king, निमिः Nimi, नाम by name, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् among the Ikshvakus, महात्मनाम् of great souls, पुत्रः son, द्वादशमः twelfth, वीर्ये in valor, धर्मे in righteousness, च and, परिनिष्ठितः firmly established
explanation: There was a king named Nimi, the twelfth son among the noble Ikshvakus, who was firmly established in both valor and righteousness.

shloka_text: स राजा वीर्यसम्पन्नः पुरं देवपुरोपमम् । निवेशयामास तदा अभ्याशे गौतमस्य तु ।। 7.55.5 ।।
transliteration: sa rājā vīryasampannaḥ puraṃ devapuropamam | niveśayāmāsa tadā abhyāśe gautamasya tu || 7.55.5 ||
translation: सः that, राजा king, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, पुरम् a city, देवपुरोपमम् resembling a city of gods, निवेशयामास established, तदा then, अभ्याशे near, गौतमस्य of Gautama, तु indeed
explanation: That valiant king then founded a city, resembling a divine city, near the hermitage of Gautama.

shloka_text: पुरस्य सुकृतं नाम वैजयन्तमिति श्रुतम् । निवेशं यत्र राजर्षिर्निमिश्चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.55.6 ।।
transliteration: purasya sukṛtaṃ nāma vaijayantamiti śrutam | niveśaṃ yatra rājarṣirnimiścakre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.55.6 ||
translation: पुरस्य of the city, सुकृतम् well-made, नाम by name, वैजयन्तम् Vaijayanta, इति thus, श्रुतम् known, निवेशम् settlement, यत्र where, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निमिः Nimi, चक्रे made, महायशाः greatly renowned
explanation: The city was known as Sukrita, or Vaijayanta, where the greatly renowned royal sage Nimi established his settlement.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य सुमहापुरम् । यजेयं दीर्घसत्रेण पितुः प्रह्लादयन्मनः ।। 7.55.7 ।।
transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya sumahāpuram | yajeyaṃ dīrghasatreṇa pituḥ prahlādayanmanaḥ || 7.55.7 ||
translation: तस्य to him, बुद्धिः thought, समुत्पन्ना arose, निवेश्य having established, सुमहापुरम् a very great city, यजेयम् I should sacrifice, दीर्घसत्रेण with a long sacrifice, पितुः of the father, प्रह्लादयन् delighting, मनः the mind
explanation: After establishing that magnificent city, the thought arose in him, "I should perform a long sacrifice, delighting my father's mind."

shloka_text: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम् । वसिष्ठं वरयामास पूर्वं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् ।। 7.55.8 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pitaramāmantrya ikṣvākuṃ hi manoḥ sutam | vasiṣṭhaṃ varayāmāsa pūrvaṃ brahmarṣisattamam || 7.55.8 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, पितरम् father, आमन्त्र्य having invited, इक्ष्वाकुम् Ikshvaku, हि indeed, मनोः of Manu, सुतम् the son, वसिष्ठम् Vasishtha, वरयामास chose, पूर्वम् first, ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् the foremost among Brahmarishis
explanation: Thereafter, having consulted his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he first chose Vasishtha, the foremost among Brahmarishis, to officiate the sacrifice.

shloka_text: अनन्तरं स राजर्षिर्निमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोधनम् ।। 7.55.9 ।।
transliteration: anantaraṃ sa rājarṣirnimirikṣvākunandanaḥ | atrimaṅgirasaṃ caiva bhṛguṃ caiva tapodhanam || 7.55.9 ||
translation: अनन्तरम् thereafter, स that, राजर्षिः royal sage, निमिः Nimi, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः descendant of Ikshvaku, अत्रिम् Atri, अङ्गिरसम् Angiras, च एव and also, भृगुम् Bhrigu, च एव and also, तपोधनम् rich in penance,
explanation: Subsequently, the royal sage Nimi, a descendant of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, who were rich in penance.

shloka_text: तमुवाच वसिष्ठस्तु निमिं राजर्षिसत्तमम् । वृतो ऽहं पूर्वमिन्द्रेण अन्तरं प्रतिपालय ।। 7.55.10 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca vasiṣṭhastu nimiṃ rājarṣisattamam | vṛto 'haṃ pūrvamindreṇa antaraṃ pratipālaya || 7.55.10 ||
translation: तम् to him, उवाच said, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, तु however, निमिम् to Nimi, राजर्षिसत्तमम् the best among royal sages, वृतः chosen, अहम् I am, पूर्वम् previously, इन्द्रेण by Indra, अन्तरम् an interval, प्रतिपालय wait for,
explanation: However, Vasishtha said to Nimi, the best of royal sages, "I have already been chosen by Indra, so please wait for some time."

shloka_text: अनन्तरं महाविप्रो गौतमः प्रत्यपूरयत् । वसिष्ठो ऽपि महातेजा इन्द्रयज्ञमथाकरोत् ।। 7.55.11 ।।
transliteration: anantaraṃ mahāvipro gautamaḥ pratyapūrayat | vasiṣṭho 'pi mahātejā indrayajñamathākarot || 7.55.11 ||
translation: अनन्तरम् thereafter, महाविप्रः the great brahmin, गौतमः Gautama, प्रत्यपूरयत् fulfilled (the request), वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, अपि also, महातेजा greatly effulgent, इन्द्रयज्ञम् Indra's sacrifice, अथ then, अकरोत् performed,
explanation: Subsequently, the great brahmin Gautama fulfilled Nimi's request, while the greatly effulgent Vasishtha then performed Indra's sacrifice.

shloka_text: निमिस्तु राजा विप्रांस्तान्समानीय नराधिपः । अयजद्धिमवत्पार्श्वे स्वपुरस्य समीपतः । पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राजा दीक्षामुपागमत् ।। 7.55.12 ।।
transliteration: nimistu rājā viprāṃstānsamānīya narādhipaḥ | ayajaddhimavatpārśve svapurasya samīpataḥ | pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi rājā dīkṣāmupāgamat || 7.55.12 ||
translation: निमिः Nimi, तु however, राजा king, विप्रान् those brahmins, तान् them, समानीय having gathered, नराधिपः the lord of men, अयजत् performed sacrifice, हिमवत्पार्श्वे on the side of the Himalayas, स्वपुरस्य of his own city, समीपतः near, पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि for five thousand years, राजा the king, दीक्षाम् the vow (of sacrifice), उपागमत् undertook,
explanation: King Nimi, the lord of men, however, gathered those brahmins and performed a sacrifice near his own city, on the side of the Himalayas, undertaking the sacrificial vow for five thousand years.

shloka_text: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने तु वसिष्ठो भगवनृषिः । सकाशमागतो राज्ञो हौत्रं कर्तुमनिन्दितः ।। 7.55.13 ।।
transliteration: indrayajñāvasāne tu vasiṣṭho bhagavanṛṣiḥ | sakāśamāgato rājño hautraṃ kartumaninditaḥ || 7.55.13 ||
translation: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, तु however, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, भगवन् divine, ऋषिः sage, सकाशम् near, आगतः came, राज्ञः of the king, हौत्रम् the role of hotri, कर्तुम् to perform, अनिन्दितः blameless,
explanation: However, at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, the blameless divine sage Vasishtha came near the king to perform the role of the hotri priest.

shloka_text: तदन्तरमथापश्यद्गौतमेनाभिपूरितम् । कोपेन महताविष्टो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।। 7.55.14 ।।
transliteration: tadantaramathāpaśyadgautamenābhipūritam | kopena mahatāviṣṭo vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 7.55.14 ||
translation: तदन्तरम् thereafter, अथ then, अपश्यत् (he) saw, गौतमेन by Gautama, अभिपूरितम् filled (the place), कोपेन with anger, महता great, आविष्टः overcome, वसिष्ठः Vasiṣṭha, ब्रह्मणः of Brahma, सुतः the son.
explanation: Then, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, saw the place occupied by Gautama and was overcome with great anger.

shloka_text: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी मुहूर्तं समुपाविशत् । तस्मिन्नहनि राजर्षिर्निद्रया ऽपहृतो भृशम् ।। 7.55.15 ।।
transliteration: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī muhūrtaṃ samupāviśat | tasminnahani rājarṣirnidrayā 'pahṛto bhṛśam || 7.55.15 ||
translation: सः He, राज्ञः of the king, दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी desirous of seeing, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, समुपाविशत् sat down, तस्मिन् on that, अहनि day, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निद्रया by sleep, अपहृतः overcome, भृशम् greatly.
explanation: Desirous of seeing the king, Vasiṣṭha sat down for a moment, but on that day, the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.

shloka_text: ततो मन्युर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः । अदर्शनेन राजर्षेर्व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.16 ।।
transliteration: tato manyurvasiṣṭhasya prādurāsīnmahātmanaḥ | adarśanena rājarṣervyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.16 ||
translation: ततः Then, मन्युः anger, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasiṣṭha, प्रादुरासीत् arose, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, अदर्शनेन by the non-seeing, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Then, anger arose in the great-souled Vasiṣṭha due to the absence of the royal sage, and he began to speak.

shloka_text: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव । चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्तव भविष्यति ।। 7.55.17 ।।
transliteration: yasmāttvamanyaṃ vṛtavānmāmavajñāya pārthiva | cetanena vinābhūto dehastava bhaviṣyati || 7.55.17 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, अन्यम् another, वृतवान् have chosen, माम् me, अवज्ञाय disregarding, पार्थिव O King, चेतनेन with consciousness, विनाभूतः devoid of, देहः body, तव your, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: "O King, because you have chosen another, disregarding me, your body will become devoid of consciousness."

shloka_text: ततः प्रबुद्धो राजर्षिः श्रुत्वा शापमुदाहृतम् । ब्रह्मयोनिमथोवाच संरम्भात् क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.55.18 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prabuddho rājarṣiḥ śrutvā śāpamudāhṛtam | brahmayonimathovāca saṃrambhāt krodhamūrcchitaḥ || 7.55.18 ||
translation: ततः Then, प्रबुद्धः awakened, राजर्षिः the royal sage, श्रुत्वा having heard, शापम् the curse, उदाहृतम् uttered, ब्रह्मयोनिम् to the one born from Brahma, अथ then, उवाच spoke, संरम्भात् from agitation, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with anger.
explanation: Then, the royal sage, awakened and having heard the uttered curse, spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, overcome with fury and anger.

shloka_text: अजानतः शयानस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः । मुक्तवान्मयि शापाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम् ।। 7.55.19 ।।
transliteration: ajānataḥ śayānasya krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ | muktavānmayi śāpāgniṃ yamadaṇḍamivāparam || 7.55.19 ||
translation: अजानतः unaware, शयानस्य of one who was sleeping, क्रोधेन by anger, कलुषीकृतः enraged, मुक्तवान् he released, मयि upon me, शापाग्निं the fire of a curse, यमदण्डम् the rod of Yama, इव like, अपरम् another.
explanation: Enraged by anger, he, unaware of me sleeping, cast upon me the fire of a curse, like a second rod of Yama.

shloka_text: तस्मात्तवापि ब्रह्मर्षे चेतनेन विना कृतः । देहः सुरुचिरप्रख्यो भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.55.20 ।।
transliteration: tasmāttavāpi brahmarṣe cetanena vinā kṛtaḥ | dehaḥ suruciraprakhyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.55.20 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, तवापि even your, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi, चेतनेन by consciousness, विना कृतः deprived of, देहः body, सुरुचिरप्रख्यो exceedingly charming in appearance, भविष्यति will be, न संशयः no doubt.
explanation: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, without a doubt, even your exceedingly charming body will be deprived of consciousness.

shloka_text: इति रोषवशादुभौ तदानीमन्योन्यं शपितौ नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ । सहसैव बभूवतुर्विदेहौ तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ ।। 7.55.21 ।।
transliteration: iti roṣavaśādubhau tadānīmanyonyaṃ śapitau nṛpadvijendrau | sahasaiva babhūvaturvidehau tattulyādhigataprabhāvavantau || 7.55.21 ||
translation: इति thus, रोषवशात् due to the power of anger, उभौ both, तदानीम् then, अन्योन्यं each other, शपितौ cursed, नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ the king and the chief of Brahmins, सहसैव suddenly, बभूवतुः became, विदेहौ bodiless, तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ possessing equally acquired power.
explanation: Thus, under the sway of anger, both the king and the chief of Brahmins, having cursed each other, suddenly became bodiless, each possessing an equally acquired power. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
